plate.narration: The rush road has stopped at the ford. Wagon wheels sink into ruts while a centaur hurries past with line tokens. Somewhere ahead, the river is deciding who gets across. First, everyone has to wait their turn.

objectives.label: Put the centaur markers back up
Helped the Bracken family get home
Shared supper with the cinder wolves

goal.text: Wait your turn at the river ford, then try to get across.

steps.label: Help someone stuck in the line
Spend the night in the line
Take your turn at the ford

facet_ford.name: The Ford Stone
facet_ford.text: Wrapped in a witch's wool sock. It rings every bell charm it passes, and won't stop.

charm_ford_witch.name: Mother Thrum's Tuned Charm
charm_ford_witch.text: A bell charm tuned to the note the stones hum. Hold it near a gem and it sings.

scene_parade.narration: Marda's rumor board said the rush road was jammed but moving. Your job tonight: wait your turn at the river ford, then get across. Wagons fill the ruts. Centaur relay-runners weave between them. Ahead, somebody shouts, "NUMBERS! GET YOUR NUMBERS!"

scene_parade_sniff_wagons.narration: Your dragonling sniffs a gem wagon and goes very still. It smells like home: warm rock, ash, a cave. Underneath is a hum you can feel in your teeth. Every wagon smells the same.

scene_parade_read_crowd.narration: Your kitsune reads the line like a menu. That wagon has jumped two places. That man is selling the same pebble twice. Soon you know the whole line's business, and the line does not know you know.

scene_spilled_pannier.narration: A wagon wheel drops into a rut, and gem chips spill everywhere. "WATCH YOUR BOOTS!" booms the lead drover, who runs the river crossing. Help him catch the chips, or stand back and watch.

check_catch_chips.prompt: Everybody scoop up the rolling gem chips before the crowd does

onSuccess.narration: You dive, scoop and pass, scoop and pass, and every chip is back in the pannier before a single pocket gets one. The drover counts them twice, then booms a thank you so loud the horses jump. He will remember your faces.

onFailure.narration: You scoop up a whole double handful, very proudly, and give the drover three chips and a great deal of gravel. He laughs so hard his hat falls off. By the time he finds it, the crowd has pocketed the rest.

scene_spilled_pannier_hold_back.narration: You stand back. The crowd scrambles and stuffs its pockets. Nobody notices what you notice: every chip in the dust is trembling, like a kettle far away.

scene_spilled_pannier_spot_all.narration: Your bigfoot looks once, and points. Under the wheel. In a hoofprint. Inside somebody's boot. Every chip goes back. "Never seen eyes like that," the drover booms. "I'll remember you folks."

scene_number_pebble.narration: At the west branch, the ford line is two days long. A faun named Burdock sells numbered pebbles and very expensive honeycakes. Your pebble says 412. "My lucky number!" he says. The ford is on number 9.

scene_number_pebble_buy_cake.narration: Three coins buy a honeycake the size of one coin. "My lucky number," says Burdock, meaning your money. You save the cake for someone who needs it.

scene_number_pebble_pocket_pebble.narration: You keep your coins and pebble 412. Burdock's goat, Pudding, stares into the pebble bucket. Nothing good starts with a goat staring into a bucket.

choice_runaway_goat.narration: Burdock's goat, Pudding, gallops down the line with the pebble bucket on her head. Numbers fly everywhere. "My bucket! My GOAT!" wails Burdock. Chase her, or sort the spilled numbers for a honeycake.

check_goat_chase.narration: Pudding gallops off with the bucket on her head. Every few steps she stops at a cabbage stall to chew. "Wait for the chew!" wails Burdock. "Then grab!"

interaction.cue: Tap when Pudding stops to chew.

onSuccess.narration: You grab the bucket just as Pudding leaps a cooking pot. She loved that game, and follows you all day. Burdock pays you three coins.

onFailure.narration: Pudding leaps a cooking pot and a sleeping drover. You leap the pot, mostly. In the end she trots back to Burdock by herself.

choice_runaway_goat_sort.narration: You ask people their numbers and sort the pebbles fairly. Burdock gives you a honeycake. "This has never happened," he says. "Tell nobody." Pudding wanders back.

choice_runaway_goat_crumb.narration: Pudding eats the crumb and drops the bucket. Then she follows you. Burdock approves of this for about one day.

scene_three_cards.narration: A kitsune named Tamsin Three-Cards shuffles cards on a barrel. "Find the Sun Card! Win a front-of-the-line pebble!" Her third tail twitches. Catch her trick, walk away, or help her fool the crowd.

check_expose.narration: Tamsin's hands blur and the cards fly. The Sun Card starts on the left. Her third tail twitches every time it moves. Watch where it goes.

interaction.cue: Watch the Sun Card, then pick its card.

onSuccess.narration: Every shuffle, her tail flicks the Sun Card up her sleeve. You say so, loudly and politely.

onFailure.narration: You pick a picture of a very smug fox. The crowd laughs, and so does she.

scene_exposed.narration: Tamsin shakes the Sun Card out of her sleeve, and the crowd gets its pebbles back. The drovers saw who caught the trick. They will wave you in beside the lead wagon at the ford.

scene_join_con.narration: You gasp loudly in the crowd every time somebody almost wins. Tamsin pays you with a wink and a shiny pebble. It says Number 1. It is not fair at all.

scene_three_cards_walk_by.narration: You keep your coins. Tamsin tips her hat. "Come back when you feel lucky." Behind you, somebody loses again, very loudly.

scene_soup_line.narration: A cheerful ladler named Wend gives away free soup under the dark-robed helpers' tent. "Kindness first," says Wend. A little crystal on the ladle cord shivers whenever a gem wagon passes.

scene_soup_line_ask_crystal.narration: "Since the red night," says Wend, lifting the crystal. "Means something, doesn't it?" Another wagon passes. The crystal hums. Wend changes the subject to soup.

scene_soup_line_thank_wend.narration: Wend beams and fills your bowls again. "Kindness first." The crystal shivers at another wagon.

scene_queue_jumpers.narration: A gang in red scarves pushes up the line. "Ford closes tomorrow!" their leader shouts. An old faun doubts it. Hold the line, and the scarves may treat you fairly later. Or fetch the drovers.

check_block_jumpers.narration: The red scarves charge up the line, elbows first. The old faun grabs your sleeve. "Link arms!" he says. Everybody braces.

interaction.cue: Friends brace the line while someone holds the front.

onSuccess.narration: You link arms with the old faun and two surprised strangers. The red scarves bounce off like a ball off a wall. The line cheers, and the old faun gives you two coins.

onFailure.narration: The red scarves squeeze past. Then the last one trips over Pudding's bucket, and the whole gang goes down in a heap. Laughed at, they slink to the back.

scene_queue_jumpers_call_drovers.narration: You fetch the lead drover. He strolls up the line, stands in front of the red scarves, and says one word. "BACK." It rattles the wagon wheels. They go back.

scene_queue_jumpers_send_back.narration: Your kitsune smiles the sweetest smile in the line. "Haven't you heard? The back is the front now." The red scarves sprint to the back. It takes them an hour to work it out.

scene_queue_jumpers_tamsin_help.narration: Tamsin strolls up, shuffling. "Find the Sun Card, win a place at the front!" The red scarves play for an hour and never find it. By then the line has rolled on without them.

scene_relay_message.narration: A centaur relay-runner skids up. "Message for the drovers! Can't stop!" The note says RIVER RISING. CROSS SLOW. Run it, sing it down the line, or fly it to the ford.

check_run_message.prompt: Run a message down a two-day line, with the fastest of you in front

onSuccess.narration: You weave through wagons, goats and campfires, and slap the note into the lead drover's hand. He reads it, nods, and slows the crossing to a careful walk. When you get back, the runner tosses you a brave whistle. "The relay remembers," she says.

onFailure.narration: You run as fast as you can and hand the note to the wrong drover, who reads it out loud to absolutely everybody. That, it turns out, works just as well. By lunchtime the whole line knows the river is rising.

scene_relay_message_sing.narration: You sing RIVER RISING, CROSS SLOW. The next fire sings it to the next. Soon the drovers sing it back. The runner grins and gallops away.

scene_relay_message_fly.narration: Your griffin crosses the whole line in four wingbeats. The lead drover reads the note and nods. Back in line, the runner whistles. "The relay could use a friend with wings."

choice_tolls.narration: Pick one job before dusk. Free a stuck wagon, and its crew will help you in the ford. Fix the marker line for an easier ford. Or help the Brackens, a faun family with a cracked wheel, and ride their cart. "We are being very brave," says Littlest Bracken.

check_unmire.prompt: Everybody heave a gem wagon out of the mud

onSuccess.narration: One, two, THREE, and the wagon comes out with a noise like a giant boot leaving a puddle. The drover gives you a brave whistle and calls you "mudlarks", which is a compliment.

onFailure.narration: The wagon comes out in the end, but only after everyone has sat down in the mud at least once. You will be finding mud in your ears until next week.

check_markers.prompt: Put the markers back in the right order

onSuccess.narration: Post by post, you walk the line back into order, reading the worn numbers with your thumbs where the paint has gone. The last marker goes in with a thump, and the whole line points, straight and plain, at the one safe way down to the ford.

onFailure.narration: You put them all back up, beautifully, in the wrong order. A centaur runner gallops past, stops, laughs, and fixes them in about four seconds.

scene_markers_restored.narration: The marker line stands straight again, every post pointing the safe way to the ford. A relay-runner slows just long enough to say, "The relay remembers."

scene_family.narration: The Brackens' cart wheel is cracked, and they need to get home before the river rises. The littlest Bracken holds a pebble with a huge number and is trying very hard not to cry.

scene_family_fix_wheel.narration: You lash the cracked wheel with rope until it looks like a wheel in a sweater. It wobbles, but it turns. The littlest Bracken calls it the best wheel ever made.

scene_family_share_cake.narration: You break the honeycake so the littlest Bracken gets a bit from everyone. For a while nobody talks, because honeycake. The littlest one falls asleep with crumbs on both cheeks.

scene_family_give_pebble.narration: You trade pebbles with the littlest Bracken. Their number was enormous. Yours was not. The littlest Bracken cries happily all over the small one. The Brackens will cross at dawn.

scene_dusk_wolves.narration: Cinder wolves sit beyond the firelight, cold and thin. They keep away from the humming gem wagons, but their ears turn at every clink of a bowl. Share your supper, let them be, or drive them off.

scene_wolves_fed.narration: You set your supper on a flat stone and step back. The wolves eat politely. Then the whole pack curls up by your fire, glowing like coals. It is the warmest night all week.

scene_dusk_wolves_leave_be.narration: You keep the fire small. The wolves stay beyond its light. At midnight one howls a long, low note. The gem wagons creak in their sleep.

encounter_wolves.narration: The wolves do not want to leave. They are cold, and your fire is right there.

onVictory.narration: The pack slinks off to the next fire, where somebody feeds them.

onDefeat.narration: The wolves eat everybody's supper and curl up on your bedrolls. Cold and hungry, you wander toward the big campfire.

scene_campfire_play.narration: At the big campfire, a troupe acts out the red night with blankets and saucepans. Their mountain gets the hiccups. "New mountain, darlings!" cries the leader. Play it, or tell them what you really heard.

check_play_mountain.narration: The troupe leader hands you a red blanket and points at a barrel. "Climb up, darling, and be a MOUNTAIN!"

interaction.cue: Rumble, wobble and erupt until the mountain is finished.

options.label: Wobble the red blanket
options.reaction: The whole front row wobbles with you.

onSuccess.narration: You RUMBLE under the red blanket and erupt with a sack of pinecones. The children shriek with joy. The leader pays you a honeycake.

onFailure.narration: You RUMBLE under the red blanket and erupt with a sack of pinecones. The children shriek with joy. The leader pays you a honeycake.

scene_campfire_play_tell_true.narration: You describe the hum in every gem. The leader changes the play. Now the mountain is quiet, and the falling stones sing. "Much spookier," she whispers.

scene_campfire_play_goat_mountain.narration: Pudding climbs the barrel, wears the red blanket, and eats the script. Her one bleat gets the loudest cheer of the night. She bows by mistake.

scene_campfire_play_rewrite.narration: Your kitsune changes the play on the spot. In the new ending, the stones are not treasure. They are a puzzle. The crowd likes it better. "Annoyingly better," mutters the leader.

scene_witch_stall.narration: At a remedy stall, bell charms ring whenever a gem wagon passes. The witch, Mother Thrum, winces over her glasses. "What do you actually want?" she asks.

scene_witch_stall_sore_feet.narration: Mother Thrum hands over a sunbloom potion. "Feet next. Listen first." Another wagon makes every charm ring. She closes her eyes and counts to three.

scene_tuned_charm.narration: Mother Thrum gives you a tuned bell charm. Near any gem, it sings the same ancient note. "Older than the road," she says. On her shelf, a stone rings inside a wool sock.

scene_tuned_charm_leave_it.narration: You leave the ringing stone in its sock. Mother Thrum tucks it behind the counter. "Some questions take longer." You head back to camp with the tuned charm.

scene_tuned_charm_take_it_home.narration: You tell her where it fell from, and that you will take it back. The ringing stops the moment the stone touches your dragonling's hands. "There," says Mother Thrum softly. "It knows. Keep it warm."

check_answer.prompt: Tell Mother Thrum what you actually want, and mean it

onSuccess.narration: Mother Thrum listens all the way to the end, then hands you the sock with the stone in it. "That's the Ford Stone. Take it somewhere it stops ringing," she says. "I'd like some sleep."

onFailure.narration: You say something about gems and glory, and Mother Thrum's charms all go quiet at once, which feels like an answer. "Not yet," she says kindly. "Ask yourself again at the mountain."

scene_charm_walk.narration: Your tuned charm sings at every passing wagon. Nearby, the wolves lie well away from the gems. Compare the wagons' notes, or test the charm on the wolves.

check_listen_charm.prompt: Hold the charm to wagon after wagon and listen for a different note

onSuccess.narration: Wagon after wagon, gem after gem, and the note never changes. Not higher. Not lower. Big gems and tiny chips all sing the very same note, as if they all came from one place. One very, very old place.

onFailure.narration: So many wagons, so much singing, that the notes blur together in your head like a choir with a cold. You will have to listen again somewhere quieter. Still, you are sure of one thing: every gem is singing.

scene_charm_walk_wolves.narration: You hold the charm out into the dark. It sings. Every wolf flattens its ears and moves ten steps farther off. They are not afraid of you. They are keeping away from the note.

scene_charm_walk_ford_stone.narration: You hold the charm against the wool sock. Charm and stone ring together, so loud that every bell in the line answers. Sleepy people sit up and say "WHAT?" Then both go quiet at once.

rest_witch_fire.narration: Rest in the line. The charm chimes at passing wagons, and Pudding visits every supper pot. At dawn, Burdock takes her home, and a drover calls numbers from much closer to the water. Your turn is nearly here.

scene_crossing_verse.narration: At dawn the lead drover sings the crossing verse: slow, slow, wait, slow. "My ford, my pace," he booms. The river is higher. Learn the verse, or study the water.

check_learn_verse.narration: The lead drover sings it again, thumping one step for each line: slow, and slow, and wait, and slow. "Now sing it back," he booms. "In order."

interaction.cue: Listen to the verse, then sing it back in order.

onSuccess.narration: By the third time through, you are singing with him. "Huh," he booms. "You've got it." The verse sits in your chest like a drum.

onFailure.narration: You learn a verse beautifully. It is the one about turnips that the drovers sing at supper.

scene_crossing_verse_watch.narration: The middle current is slower. At the west edge it pulls toward the marsh. A slip there means a different road.

scene_crossing_verse_drover_teaches.narration: "Mudlarks! Over here!" The lead drover teaches you each line until you can echo it. His eyebrows conduct the whole lesson. Now you know the crossing verse.

choice_ford.narration: The river is wide and fast. "One wagon at a time," booms the lead drover. The jobs you did in the line can help now. How will you cross?

check_ford.prompt: Keep your footing in the ford

onSuccess.narration: Step, wait, step. The water pushes and pulls and you do not let it. The lead drover sings the last line of the verse just as your boots hit the north bank.

onFailure.narration: Halfway across, somebody behind you shouts, and then everybody behind you shouts, and the water that was pushing at your knees is suddenly pushing at your waist.

check_ford_easy.prompt: Link arms and wade across together, nice and steady

onSuccess.narration: With friends on every side, the ford is just very wet walking. Somebody up on a wagon starts clapping as you reach the north bank.

onFailure.narration: You are nearly across, with friends on every side, when a yell goes up behind you and the whole river seems to lurch at once.

scene_surge.narration: Halfway across, the red scarves charge into the water behind you, and a bread wagon tips over with a SPLASH. Two river drakes pop up, very interested in the bread. The current shoves at your knees.

variants.text: Tamsin's pebble still says Number 1. Nobody down here is checking numbers.

check_drake_toll.prompt: Fish the floating loaves out of the river and toss each drake its share

onSuccess.narration: The drakes take the bread like a toll collector takes coins, and one of them even nudges the wagon back onto its wheels with its nose. Drovers haul you up the north bank by your collars.

onFailure.narration: One drake takes the bread. The other one wanted the bread you were holding, and it bumps you, very gently, into the deep part.

encounter_drakes.narration: The drakes do not see why a wagon full of bread should stay upright when it could be lunch.

onVictory.narration: The drakes sulk off with one loaf each. The drovers cheer as you shove the wagon up the bank.

onDefeat.narration: A drake flicks its tail. Over goes the wagon, and you go with it, into the current.

scene_surge_scarves_help.narration: "HEY, RED SCARVES!" you shout. Their leader shrugs. "Fair's fair." The whole gang wades in, and together you heave the wagon upright while the drakes squabble over bread.

end_forded.narration: You stand dripping on the north bank, with the whole rush pouring past toward the mountain. The tuned charm chimes at every wagon. Behind you, the crossing verse starts again. Tonight you camp on the north side, right in the thick of it.

variants.text: The drover helped with your chip line.
The runner helped check your marker line.
The wagon crew repaid your line work.
The Brackens helped balance your ride across.

end_marsh_west.narration: The west branch whooshes you into the Whispering Marsh, past a boggart in a reed hat who claps. You wash up near MossHome, the bigfoot town, at the edge of the Enchanted Woods. Not the road you planned, but the charm still hums.

variants.text: The drover helped with your chip line.
The runner helped check your marker line.
The wagon crew repaid your line work.
The Brackens helped balance your ride across.

end_swept_setback.narration: The current takes you a long way west, through the marsh, three days late. You wash up at the flooded edge of the Enchanted Woods with wet bags and a grudge against drakes. It cost you time, but the charm still hums.

variants.text: The drover helped with your chip line.
The runner helped check your marker line.
The wagon crew repaid your line work.
The Brackens helped balance your ride across.

scene_reed_crabs.narration: Two young glassback crabs have parked on the first crossing stones. Wheels come close. Claws click. Wheels back away. "Back to the reeds, please," booms the lead drover. The crabs ignore him.

encounter_crabs.narration: The crabs clack and shuffle sideways, in no hurry at all. Nudge them off the stones before the line loses patience.

scene_crabs_cleared.narration: The crabs shuffle back to the reeds like small dukes leaving a party. The drover gives you a river charm. "Polite neighbors," he booms, and begins his verse.

scene_crabs_coaxed.narration: The crabs won't move until the drover tips bread crusts down the bank. Off they scuttle. No river charm, but the first step is clear.

interaction_soup_bowls.narration: Near the soup tent, empty bowls are rolling out of a basket into the mud. Catch each bowl and stack it before the next hungry traveler arrives.

interaction.cue: Tap when a bowl reaches the basket rim.

interaction_clear_lane.narration: Hoofbeats race down the line. A relay-runner needs a clear lane, but a loose awning sags across the road. Hold its pole up while people duck clear.

interaction.cue: Friends brace the pole while someone lifts the awning.

interaction_evening_echo.narration: As camp settles, travelers tap a welcome on their bowls: tap, tap, rest, tap. Listen, or join in. At last the road stops telling everyone to hurry.

interaction_dawn_warmup.narration: Morning is cold enough to make boots creak. The waiting travelers turn warming up into a game. Stamp, stretch, and shake the sleep out of your fingers.

interaction_chip_line.narration: You hold the pannier while the drover gathers his chips. He counts the last handful, then booms a thank you so loud the horses jump. He will remember your faces.

interaction_wagon_level.narration: The stuck wagon leans hard into its rut. Raise or lower your side of the load until it sits level, then roll it out. The drover has named the rut. "Do not encourage it."

interaction.cue: Raise or lower your side until the wagon load is level.

onSuccess.narration: Level at last! The wagon rolls out with an enormous squelch. The drover's crew will help you if a wagon tips in the ford.

onFailure.narration: The wagon comes out, but only after everyone sits down in the mud at least once.

onAssisted.narration: The drover props the wheel while you level the load. The wagon rolls free, and he promises his crew's help in the ford.

interaction_ford_posts.narration: The marker posts have fallen flat. Brace the ropes while a friend raises them, or use the support prop. One arrow points into a cabbage stall. A relay-runner fixes that one herself.

interaction.cue: Brace the ropes while the acting hero raises the marker line.

onSuccess.narration: The arrows stand along the safe approach. The runner gives them one last look and nods.

onFailure.narration: The post leans over again. The runner fixes the line, but you did not check the approach yourselves.

onAssisted.narration: The runner takes one rope while you raise the posts. You check the safe approach together.

interaction_bracken_crossing.narration: The Brackens saved you a place. Their cart rocks into the ford. Keep its load level while the lead drover calls the slow steps. The littlest Bracken holds the bread. It is an important job.

interaction.cue: Raise or lower your side to level the Brackens' cart.
interaction.actionLabel: Bring the cart to the bank

onSuccess.narration: The cart reaches the north bank level. The littlest Bracken lifts the bread in triumph.

onFailure.narration: Another wagon tips behind you, and the cart rocks sideways. The drovers grab the reins. Now you face the surge.

onAssisted.narration: Mother Bracken shifts the sacks while you balance the cart. You cross with the family's help.

interaction_surge_brace.narration: The wagon crew you freed wades up with a long brace. Hold it steady while one of you guides the wheel upright. The drakes argue over the bread.

interaction.cue: Hold the brace while the acting hero rights the wagon.

onSuccess.narration: The brace holds. Your crew rights the wheel, and everyone reaches the north bank.

onFailure.narration: The wheel slips past the brace. The crew pulls you free, but the current takes you west.

onAssisted.narration: The lead drover anchors the brace beside the crew. Together you right the load and reach the bank.

interaction_dawn_warmup_response_shake.narration: Somebody wiggles all ten fingers at the river.

voiceGuide.tone: busy, loud, funny road-camp country; warm underneath, a little spooky at dusk, never scary

npcVoices.burdock: a faun provisioner; cheerful, shameless about his prices, calls everyone 'my lucky number'; owns Pudding, a goat with a weakness for buckets
npcVoices.tamsin: Tamsin Three-Cards, a kitsune card-sharp; quick, delighted to be caught, never sore about losing
npcVoices.wend: a Deep Hollow soup ladler; gentle, generous, asks nothing, says 'kindness first' and means it a little too much
npcVoices.mother_thrum: a ford witch; careful and instructive, peers over glasses, always asks 'what do you actually want?'
npcVoices.drover: the lead drover; slow, booming voice, sings the crossing verse and will not be hurried
npcVoices.relay_runner: a centaur relay-runner; talks while galloping, never finishes a sentence in the same place she started it
npcVoices.brackens: the Brackens, a faun family whose season is over; tired, polite, the littlest one very brave about it
npcVoices.troupe_leader: a rush-camp actor-manager; grand and dramatic, calls everyone 'darlings', thrilled by any eruption
npcVoices.red_scarves: the red-scarf line-cutters' leader; pushy and impatient, but fair when fairly beaten

interaction_chip_line.narration: The chips roll toward the rut. Catch the pannier at your place, then pass it along while the drover gathers the spill. Alone, catch and hand it straight to him. The dog has volunteered to count. Nobody has accepted.

interaction.cue: Catch the pannier, then pass it along the line.

onSuccess.narration: You dive, scoop and pass, scoop and pass, and every chip is back in the pannier before a single pocket gets one. The drover counts them twice, then booms a thank you so loud the horses jump. He will remember your faces.

onFailure.narration: You scoop up a whole double handful, very proudly, and give the drover three chips and a great deal of gravel. He laughs so hard his hat falls off. By the time he finds it, the crowd has pocketed the rest.

onAssisted.narration: The drover anchors the end of your line. Together you catch the spill before it reaches the crowd. He remembers the help, including his own part.

interaction_evening_echo.narration: The camp settles into evening. At the last fire before the remedy stalls, travelers tap a little welcome on their bowls: tap, tap, rest, tap. Listen, then tap it back so the next fire can hear.

interaction.cue: Listen, then repeat the welcome in order.

interaction_dawn_warmup.narration: Morning is cold enough to make every boot creak. Before anyone heads down to the ford, the waiting travelers turn warming up into a game. Stamp, stretch and shake the sleep out of your fingers.

options.label: Shake out your fingers
options.reaction: Somebody wiggles all ten fingers at the river.
